description: This case study is the HSE's Buncefield page, gathering the response to the explosions and fire at the Buncefield Oil Storage Depot in Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire, in the early hours of Sunday 11 December 2005. At least one of the initial explosions was of massive proportions and a large fire engulfed much of the site and burned for several days, emitting large clouds of black smoke; over 40 people were injured, there were no fatalities, property nearby was damaged and a large area was evacuated on emergency service advice. The Health and Safety Executive and the Environment Agency investigated and secured convictions against five companies, who were ordered to pay almost 10 million pounds in fines and costs. The page links the Major Incident Investigation Board reports, the Process Safety Leadership Group final report on safety and environmental standards for fuel storage sites, a ten-years-on report and research reports on land use planning, societal risk, layers of protection for tank overfill, explosion mechanisms and vapour cloud formation. Access: pages and PDFs, free; the page footer states the Open Government Licence v3.0. Caveats: a listing of reports, some held at the National Archives. It suits explosion consequence and land use planning studies, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
